1. through - connects the verb "drove" to the noun phrase "the city"
2. past - connects the verb "drove" to the noun phrase "the bustling markets and quiet neighborhoods"
3. on - connects the verb "reflecting" to the noun phrase "the years"
4. she - (Note: "she" is a pronoun, not a preposition. The preposition here is implied or part of the relative clause structure, but strictly speaking, there is no preposition connecting "years" to "she spent" other than the relative pronoun "that/which" which is omitted. However, looking at "spent there", "there" is an adverb. Let's re-evaluate "reflecting on". "On" is the preposition.)
5. of - connects the noun phrase "the first three months" to the noun phrase "the year"
